`@synap-core/sdk` is a typed tRPC client for a Synap pod. Every procedure the pod exposes is available with
autocomplete and compile-time checks, because the client is typed with the pod's own router type.

## What you need

- A pod: [hosted](/docs/start/cloud-quickstart) or [self-hosted](/docs/start/self-host-quickstart).
- An API key for it. See [API keys](/docs/build/api-keys).
- The ID of the workspace you want to read.

## 1. Install

```bash
npm install @synap-core/sdk
```

For a React app, install the React bindings instead; they include the SDK:

```bash
npm install @synap-core/react
```

## 2. Create a client

```ts
import { createSynapClient } from "@synap-core/sdk";

const synap = createSynapClient({
  podUrl: "https://pod.example.com", // no trailing slash, no /trpc
  apiKey: process.env.SYNAP_API_KEY,
  workspaceId: process.env.SYNAP_WORKSPACE_ID!,
});
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `podUrl` | Base URL of the pod. The client calls `<podUrl>/trpc`. |
| `apiKey` | Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. |
| `sessionToken` | A sign-in session token, sent as `x-session-token`. Takes priority over `apiKey`. For apps where a person signs in. |
| `workspaceId` | Sent as `x-workspace-id` to scope requests. Pass `""` for procedures that need no workspace. |
| `extraHeaders` | Added to every request. |
| `onAuthError` | Called on `401`. The client then rejects with a clean tRPC error instead of a parse error. |

With neither `apiKey` nor `sessionToken`, the client sends the browser's cookies (`credentials: "include"`), for an
app served next to the pod where the person is already signed in.

## 3. Read entities

```ts
const { items, pagination } = await synap.entities.list.query({ limit: 20 });

for (const entity of items) {
  console.log(entity.id, entity.title);
}
```

`entities.list` takes `limit` (1 to 1000, default 50) and `offset`, and filters such as `profileSlug` (one kind, for
example `"task"`) and `facetSlug` (one role). With a workspace set, it returns that workspace's entities.

## 4. Write, and expect proposals

```ts
const result = await synap.entities.create.mutate({
  profileSlug: "note",
  title: "My first note",
});
```

Writes go through the pod's governance. Depending on who the key belongs to and the rules you set, a write is applied
directly or comes back as a **proposal** (`status: "proposed"` with a `proposalId`) that a person approves. Handle
both. See [Validation policy](/docs/build/concepts/validation-policy).

## React

```tsx
import { SynapProvider, useSynap } from "@synap-core/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <SynapProvider podUrl="https://pod.example.com" apiKey={key} workspaceId={workspaceId}>
      <Entities />
    </SynapProvider>
  );
}

function Entities() {
  const { data } = useSynap().entities.list.useQuery({ limit: 20 });
  return <ul>{data?.items.map((e) => <li key={e.id}>{e.title}</li>)}</ul>;
}
```

`@synap-core/react` also exports ready-made `RouterInputs` and `RouterOutputs` types, and the hooks `useEntity`,
`useEntities`, `useLinks` and `useView`. `@synap-core/sdk` exports `createSynapClient` and the types `SynapClient`,
`SynapClientOptions` and `AppRouter`.

## Not using TypeScript or tRPC?

- Scripts and agents: [`@synap-core/hub-rest-client`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@synap-core/hub-rest-client), a
  zero-dependency client for the [Hub REST API](/docs/reference/hub-api), or plain HTTP.
